# `Update`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Updater: installation progress stage or failure while applying a firmware package.

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | event (device sends) |
| Grade | PURE GETTER (observation only) |
| Side-effect tier | B |
| Confidence | READ |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.31, updater socket_json_server::NotifyUpdate @0x12c00, socket_json_server_binary::NotifyUpdate @0x28140 and RefreshUpdateStatus @0x116b0 (64-bit build); 32-bit counterparts present |

Sent while the updater runs the firmware update script: a status reader watches the script output, matches progress markers and sends one event per matched stage (not periodic, no numeric percent). 64-bit polling sleeps 200 ms in the normal loop, 100 ms on the pending/abort check and 50 ms while draining a terminal or error state. Sent by the updater process (zwoair_updater) on its TCP 4350 JSON server, not by the imager. Delivered with an IP-matched send: every 4350 connection whose IP string equals the target's receives it, so several sockets from one host can all match, and other clients get nothing. State is caller-supplied: working for progress, fail on failure (READ); code and error are added on the failure branch. The packaged update scripts on both builds report the stages copy file, write disk, update mount FW and restart server; desc can also carry other dynamically parsed progress text, so it is not a closed enum. The updater records result codes 201 (receive failure), 204 (timeout) and 525 (interruption, MD5 failure or signature failure) (READ); that these reach code is INFERRED. Firmware 9.75 (64-bit build, READ for the codes, which also exist in 9.31) ends a failed update with the failure notification carrying the strings fail and error and a numeric code of 204 (900 s timeout), 529 (update error status) or 207 (update output file not found, poll aborted before it appeared, or the done marker could not be written); which wire members carry those strings is INFERRED to be state and error, and the code member the number. In 9.75 the failure path also clears the legacy update directory and writes the done marker. Other failure error and code values are unresolved. Android app consumer (READ, consumer expectation, not firmware behaviour): the legacy firmware screen selects UI by desc and also handles retry mount FW update, which no 9.31 firmware binary emits (READ, exhaustive search for absence). The newer app OTA workflow listens for OtaUpdate; no emitter for it was found in either packaged updater build.

Side effects: Observation only for the receiver.

## Request params

None. Events are sent by the device without a request; the payload is below.

## Payload

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Event` | string | yes | - | Discriminator. Fixed value `"Update"`. [READ] |
| `Timestamp` | string | yes | - | Decimal string <seconds>.<nine digits> from clock id 1 (monotonic, INFERRED); not a calendar time. [READ] |
| `state` | string | yes | - | Installation state: working during progress, fail on failure. Supplied by the caller; not an F lifecycle enum. [READ] |
| `desc` | string | yes | - | Stage description, e.g. copy file, write disk, update mount FW, restart server, or other parsed progress text. [READ] |
| `error` | string | if state is fail | - | Failure message. [READ] |
| `code` | integer | if state is fail | - | Failure code. The updater records 201 (receive failure), 204 (timeout) and 525 (interrupted, MD5 or signature failure); that these reach this member is INFERRED. Firmware 9.75 status poll failures use 204 (900 s timeout), 529 (update error) and 207 (update output missing, aborted, or done marker write failed); READ for the numbers, INFERRED for the member. Other values unresolved. [READ] |
| `route` | array<string> | yes | - | Always an empty array, inserted by the IP-matched sender; the recipient IP is not a route element. [READ] |

## Errors

None. Failures appear in the payload (`code`, `error`) when `state` is `fail`.

## Example

Event, write-disk - READ illustration shape (not captured):

```json
{"Event":"Update","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","state":"working","desc":"write disk","route":[]}
```

Event, failed - Static example of the failure branch (READ shape, not captured; code and text invented):

```json
{"Event":"Update","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","state":"fail","desc":"update mount FW","error":"example failure text","code":1,"route":[]}
```
